text.title: Competitor Analysis Examples
text.summary: End-to-end worked example illustrating the methodology against a realistic input. Folds in the former examples file: Two worked examples (note-taking app, email marketing) and a common-mistakes table showing the correct fix for each failure mode. The common mistakes now live in `content/03-failure-modes.xml`.

example.title: Note-taking app positioning
example.note: Category: PKM. Geography: US,DE,GB. Seed list from interviews + Reddit r/PKMS + Product Hunt: 6 direct (Notion, Obsidian, Roam, Logseq, Mem, Anytype), 4 indirect (Apple Notes, Google Docs, Bear, OneNote), 2 future (Cursor + ChatGPT memory). Matrix: Notion premium-broad, Obsidian budget-broad, Roam premium-narrow. Empty quadrant: budget-narrow. Parallel fan-out: 12 Task calls; each pulls pricing + 1-star G2 + Reddit thread. Weaknesses: Notion 'too slow' (n=320), Obsidian 'steep learning curve' (n=180), Roam 'expensive + dated UI'. Gap = experience. Positioning: 'For busy professionals who want fast, simple notes with linking. Unlike Notion, we are single-purpose and lightning fast. Unlike Obsidian, we work great out of the box.'

example.title: Positioning statement template
example.code: For solo freelancers Who need simple project tracking TaskLite is a project management tool That focuses on single-person workflows Unlike Asana or Monday We have no team features, just personal productivity
example.note: Naming the competitor makes the claim testable and immediately clear to the target customer. This is the canonical template form required by rule positioning-statement-template.

example.title: Note-taking app matrix
example.note: Market: personal knowledge management. Competitors analysed: Notion, Obsidian, Roam Research (direct); Apple Notes, Google Docs (indirect); AI writing tools (future).
example.code:
| Competitor | Strength | Weakness | Opportunity | |------------|------------------|-----------------------|-----------------------| | Notion | All-in-one | Slow, complex | Speed, simplicity | | Obsidian | Local-first | Steep learning curve | Easier onboarding | | Roam | Backlinks | Expensive, dated UI | Better UX, lower price|
Positioning: "For busy professionals who want fast, simple notes with linking. Unlike Notion, we're single-purpose and lightning fast. Unlike Obsidian, we work great out of the box."
example.note: Gap chosen: experience gap (speed and simplicity). Messaging names specific competitors to make the claim credible.

example.title: Email marketing for solopreneurs
example.note: Gap discovered through pricing analysis: all tools price by subscriber count, creating early paywalls for solopreneurs under 1000 subscribers.
example.code: Opportunity: "Generous free tier (5000 subscribers), solo-focused features, no team complexity" Gap type: Price gap + audience gap — no tool focuses on sub-1000 subscriber solo operators.
example.note: Price gap and audience gap combined. Competitor pricing analysis identified the tier ladder, not just features.
